correctness.rationale: The j-th generation mean density is q^j times the Erlang(mj,β) density by convolution; summing gives the stated transform and absolutely convergent series, with total mass q/(1−q). In dimensionless time the m=1 exponential is strictly decreasing and the m=2 derivative changes sign once at tanh(sqrt(q)τ)=sqrt(q). For m=3, the three cube-root poles give the stated damped sine/cosine expression. Its time derivative equals β²a(1+a)exp(−(1+a/2)τ)/3 times the frozen F(θ), with a=q^(1/3). For θ>0 the divisor exp(sqrt(3)θ)−cosθ is positive; h has limit 1 at zero and cannot exceed the positive level δ on nonpositive-sine intervals. On each positive half-wave the numerator H in h′ has derivative −4 exp(sqrt(3)θ) sinθ, strictly negative. Hence the first lobe is decreasing, and every later lobe has one strictly nondegenerate maximum d_j. Two crossings when δ<d_j add exactly one strict peak; equality is a quadratic zero of the rate derivative with negative coefficient, so the rate has a stationary inflection, not a maximum. Shift by 2π strictly decreases h on positive-sine angles, proving strict ordering; exponential decay gives finiteness for each q<1. The maximum angle is 2πj+π/6+O(exp(−2πsqrt(3)j)) from the root equation near its simple undamped zero. Thus d_j is asymptotic to (sqrt(3)/2) exp(−sqrt(3)(2πj+π/6)); 1−q_j is asymptotic to 6d_j. This holds for the ensemble descendant rate excluding the seed, not for realized catalog peaks.

value.rationale: A mode count for a delayed branching mean intensity is a natural qualitative question; the proof finds the first integer stage supporting a secondary peak and classifies all additional peaks, including the equality boundary. It supplies neither a seismic catalog fit nor a prediction of sample-path peaks.
